anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De Oratione exists (only copyrighted Greer/O'Meara/Oulton-Chadwick); nothing to compare against. Sense checked against the Greek and cited Scripture wording.

apparatus: Job 7:1 trial-word; Ps 17:30 LXX; 1 Cor 10:13; Eph 6:12 two wrestlings.
Song 2:9-10 nets resolution: not untempted but undefeated.
Rom 1:22-28 handing-over; Num 11 satiety-therapy; Isa 4:4; Mal 3:2.

choices.why: Job's noun is testing-ground, distinct from peirasmos-temptation; the paradox needs both terms visible.
apemphasis = ill-sounding statement; Origen 'looses' textual knots — keep the acoustic image.
Num 11 LXX's 'be cholera to you': meat becomes bile — the cure-by-satiety hinges on the pun.

pass_a_gloss: The treatise's climax: all life a trial, so 'bring us not in' means not undefeated-entry — the snared entered, Christ stoops through nets to them. Catalog of estates (poor/rich/healthy/sick/glorified) proves universal temptation; apostles unheard warns inferiors. God 'brings in' by handing over (Rom 1) as physician: quick cure breeds relapse, so lust is glutted to loathing (Num 11 month of meat), passions/fire/prison cleanse to willing good, Pharaoh hardened to confession. Temptations manifest hidden roots (Eve to Joseph); prepared intervals plus foreknown grace complete the defense.
